meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 4: Client Concepts
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: The user presses Escape and the elicitation dialog closes. Which action does the client report?

options.text: cancel, with no content field
decline, with no content field
No response at all: the client simply never retries
accept, with an empty content object

questions.explanation: The three-action model distinguishes accept (explicit submit, content only in form mode), decline (an explicit no) and cancel (dismissed without choosing). Servers must handle all three.

questions.question: A client sends clientCapabilities: {} and calls a tool that must ask the user a question. What does the server return?

options.text: A result with isError: true explaining that elicitation is unavailable
-32021 MissingRequiredClientCapability with data.requiredCapabilities, and HTTP 400
An InputRequiredResult anyway, letting the client decide whether it can comply
-32602 Invalid params, because the capabilities object is effectively missing

questions.explanation: The request is structurally valid, so it is not -32602; the missing piece is a capability, which is -32021 with the list in data.requiredCapabilities. A server MUST NOT send an input request type the client has not declared.

questions.question: What is the status of sampling and roots in 2026-07-28?

options.text: Deprecated for servers but still required for clients to implement
Deprecated but functional, reachable only through MRTR input requests
Active: they are the two client features alongside elicitation
Removed: servers must migrate to tool parameters and provider APIs immediately

questions.explanation: SEP-2577 deprecated Roots, Sampling and Logging in 2026-07-28; they remain functional during the window, with earliest removal in the first revision released on or after 2027-07-28. While they exist, servers reach them as MRTR inputRequests, never as server-initiated requests.

questions.question: Your client receives an InputRequiredResult for tools/call id 1, collects the user's answer, and retries. Which retry is conformant?

options.text: A new request with id 2, the original params, inputResponses, and requestState echoed exactly
A new request with id 1, so the server can correlate it with the original call
A new request with id 2 and inputResponses only, since requestState is server-side state
A notifications/input_provided message carrying the answers for request id 1

questions.explanation: The retry is an independent request and MUST use a different JSON-RPC id; correlation happens through requestState, which the client MUST echo byte for byte when the server sent one and MUST NOT invent when it did not.

questions.question: On which requests may a server return resultType: "input_required"?

options.text: Any request, provided the client declared the elicitation capability
tools/call and tools/list, the two tool-related requests
Any request except server/discover
tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get only

questions.explanation: Servers MAY send an InputRequiredResult on prompts/get, resources/read and tools/call, and MUST NOT send one on any other request. Seeing input_required on tools/list or server/discover is a conformance bug.

questions.question: A server needs the user's third-party API key to finish a tool call. Which elicitation is conformant?

options.text: Form mode, because only form mode supports schema validation of the value
Either mode, as long as the client declared support for the one chosen
Form mode with a string field marked sensitive, so the client can mask it
URL mode, so the secret never passes through the MCP client

questions.explanation: Servers MUST NOT use form mode to request passwords, API keys, access tokens or payment credentials, and MUST use URL mode for those. URL mode keeps the secret out of the client and the model's context entirely.

questions.question: A URL-mode elicitation comes back with action: "accept". What does the server actually know?

options.text: That the client fetched the URL and validated the response on the user's behalf
That the out-of-band interaction completed successfully
That the user consented to open the URL, not that the out-of-band step finished
That the user completed the flow and the client captured the resulting credential

questions.explanation: accept signals consent to the interaction. The interaction happens out of band and the client is not informed of its outcome; on the retry the server decides from its own state or the echoed requestState whether to finish or ask again. Clients MUST NOT pre-fetch the URL.

questions.question: A tool wants to elicit an order: a customer name plus a list of line items, each with a product and a quantity. What does the elicitation schema allow?

options.text: Any JSON Schema at all, so the nested array of objects can be requested exactly as it stands
Nested objects but not arrays, so the line items must become numbered fields
Only a flat object of primitive properties, so the nested list has to be restructured
Only a single string field, with any structure parsed out of it by the server

questions.explanation: Elicitation schemas are deliberately restricted to a flat object whose properties are primitives such as string, number, boolean and enum, so that any client can render them as a simple form. Complex input is collected in stages or passed as tool arguments instead.
